title: "Model card"
subtitle: "What the models do, how they were tested, and how well they work"
---

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
snapshot = FileAttachment("data/snapshot.json").json()
labels = ({majority: "Majority class", recency: "Recency rule", logreg: "Logistic regression",
  lightgbm: "LightGBM", mlp: "MLP", gru: "GRU over the last 20 matches",
  lightgbm_gru: "LightGBM + GRU average"})
ci = (v, c) => c ? `${v.toFixed(3)} (${c[0].toFixed(3)}–${c[1].toFixed(3)})` : v.toFixed(3)
signed = (x) => `${x >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(x).toFixed(3)}`
```

## Task

For a ranked player who played at least once in the 28 days before a cutoff date, predict
whether they will play **no game at all, in any queue, in the 28 days after it**. Every feature
uses only data from before the cutoff; a test deletes everything after it and checks that no
feature changes.

## Data and testing

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<p>The models learned from <strong>${snapshot.train.examples.toLocaleString()}</strong>
examples (${snapshot.train.players.toLocaleString()} players at two earlier cutoffs,
${(100 * snapshot.train.churn_rate).toFixed(1)}% churn). They are tested on
<strong>${snapshot.meta.players.toLocaleString()}</strong> other players, held out completely,
at the cutoff of ${snapshot.meta.cutoff}, when every training label was already known.</p>`
```

Model choices (regularisation, boosting rounds, network size and length of training, and the
calibration that turns scores into probabilities) were all made by cross-validation inside the
training players. The test set chose nothing.

## Results

95% bootstrap intervals in parentheses.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<table class="table table-sm">
  <thead><tr><th>Model</th><th>PR-AUC</th><th>ROC-AUC</th><th>Brier</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>${Object.entries(snapshot.metrics).map(([k, r]) => html`<tr>
    <td>${labels[k] ?? k}</td><td>${ci(r.pr_auc, r.pr_auc_ci)}</td>
    <td>${ci(r.roc_auc, r.roc_auc_ci)}</td><td>${ci(r.brier, r.brier_ci)}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
</table>`
```

**Against the recency rule** (ranking by days since the last game), on the same resamples:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<ul>${Object.entries(snapshot.vs_recency).map(([k, c]) => {
  const [lo, hi] = c.pr_auc_diff_ci
  const verdict = lo > 0 ? "beats it" : hi < 0 ? "is worse" : "is not clearly better"
  return html`<li>${labels[k] ?? k} ${verdict}: ${signed(c.pr_auc_diff)} PR-AUC
    (${signed(lo)} to ${signed(hi)})</li>`
})}</ul>`
```

## By region and tier

Does it work as well everywhere? Each group has only 15 to 75 players who stopped, so read
these for large gaps, not small ones. Tier is recorded when players were sampled and is never a
feature.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
groupRows = {
  const g = snapshot.by_group ?? {}
  const regions = {na1: "NA", euw1: "EUW", kr: "KR"}
  const tiers = ["IRON", "BRONZE", "SILVER", "GOLD", "PLATINUM", "EMERALD", "DIAMOND"]
  return [
    ...Object.keys(g.region ?? {}).sort().map((k) => ({group: regions[k] ?? k, ...g.region[k]})),
    ...tiers.filter((t) => g.tier?.[t]).map((t) => ({group: t.charAt(0) + t.slice(1).toLowerCase(), ...g.tier[t]}))
  ]
}
num = (v) => v === null || v === undefined ? "n/a" : v.toFixed(3)
html`<table class="table table-sm">
  <thead><tr><th>Group</th><th>Players</th><th>Stopped</th><th>PR-AUC LightGBM</th>
    <th>PR-AUC recency</th><th>ROC-AUC LightGBM</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>${groupRows.map((r) => html`<tr><td>${r.group}</td><td>${r.examples}</td>
    <td>${(100 * r.churned / r.examples).toFixed(0)}%</td><td>${num(r.lightgbm.pr_auc)}</td>
    <td>${num(r.recency.pr_auc)}</td><td>${num(r.lightgbm.roc_auc)}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
</table>`
```

<p class="small-note">PR-AUC depends on how many players in the group stop, so compare
LightGBM with the recency rule within a row, not across rows.</p>

## Are the probabilities right?

When LightGBM says 30%, about 30% of those players should stop. The chart groups the test
players into ten equal-sized bins by predicted probability.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bins = {
  const sorted = [...snapshot.players].sort((a, b) => a.churn - b.churn)
  const size = Math.ceil(sorted.length / 10)
  return d3.range(10).map((i) => {
    const group = sorted.slice(i * size, (i + 1) * size)
    return {predicted: d3.mean(group, (p) => p.churn), observed: d3.mean(group, (p) => +p.churned), n: group.length}
  })
}
Plot.plot({
  width: 420,
  height: 380,
  marginLeft: 48,
  marginBottom: 44,
  x: {label: "Predicted chance of stopping", labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 38,
    domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: "%", grid: true},
  y: {label: "Share who stopped", domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: "%", grid: true},
  style: {background: "transparent", color: "#52514e", fontSize: "13px"},
  marks: [
    Plot.line([[0, 0], [1, 1]], {stroke: "#c3c2b7", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.line(bins, {x: "predicted", y: "observed", stroke: "#2a78d6", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(bins, {x: "predicted", y: "observed", r: 5, fill: "#2a78d6", stroke: "#fcfcfb", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.tip(bins, Plot.pointer({x: "predicted", y: "observed",
      title: (d) => `Predicted ${(100 * d.predicted).toFixed(0)}%, observed ${(100 * d.observed).toFixed(0)}% (${d.n} players)`}))
  ]
})
```

<p class="small-note">The dashed line is perfect calibration.</p>

## The models

- **Majority class:** predicts the overall churn rate for everyone. The floor.
- **Recency rule:** ranks players by days since their last game. The bar to beat.
- **Logistic regression** and **LightGBM** on 21 features: weekly game counts, days since the
  last game, and statistics from the last 20 matches (win rate, losing streak, KDA, game
  length, queue mix, champion variety, gaps between games, session length).
- **MLP** on the same features, and a **GRU** that reads the last 20 matches one by one.
- Probabilities are Platt-calibrated on out-of-fold predictions.
- Never used as features: ladder wins, losses, LP or tier, which are measured at collection
  time, after the cutoff.

## Limitations

- Players were sampled from the ranked ladder in October 2026, which under-represents players
  who quit before the current split.
- NA, EUW and KR only, Iron to Diamond, and three cutoffs from one season.
- "Stopped" means no game for 28 days; some of these players come back later.
- With 200 churners in the test set, differences of a few points of PR-AUC can't be resolved.
  A forward test with about three times as many is scored after 2026-11-19.
